name: Time to First Token
tagline: Learn LLM inference serving by shipping one service — a 10-week, 30-minutes-a-day roadmap
description: Time to First Token is a 10-week, 30-minutes-a-day learning roadmap for engineers who want to actually run LLM inference in production, not just read about it. Fifty sessions feed a single artifact: an OpenAI-compatible inference service that you deploy on a rented GPU, instrument, load test past 1000 concurrent requests, optimize with quantization and speculative decoding, put a cost-aware router in front of, and publish as a reproducible benchmark. The curriculum covers vLLM, SGLang, quantization, speculative decoding, and Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) pruning, and assumes only comfort with Python and transformers at the architecture level — no prior serving, Kubernetes, or CUDA experience required. By the end you have a serving stack you configured, instrumented, and tuned yourself, with Grafana dashboards showing TTFT, inter-token latency, throughput, queue depth, and cost per request, plus a load-test harness and a published benchmark writeup.
highlights: 10-week, 30-minutes-a-day roadmap with 50 sessions feeding one real inference service
Covers vLLM, SGLang, quantization, speculative decoding, and TTFT pruning
Deploy, instrument, and load test past 1000 concurrent requests on a rented GPU
Grafana dashboards for TTFT, inter-token latency, throughput, queue depth, and cost
No prior serving, Kubernetes, or CUDA experience required to begin
curatorNote: The best answer I have seen to 'how do I actually learn LLM serving'. Instead of seventeen disconnected experiments, you build one growing service and learn everything through it — the single-artifact approach forces real depth and leaves you with something deployable and publishable at the end. Rarely is a learning roadmap this concrete.
